last_message:
Added `logout(member_id)` to `larder/sessions.py:19-37`, tests in `tests/test_sessions.py`, and documented it in `docs/features/sessions.md`.

Since a session cookie is a self-contained, stateless HMAC token with no way to delete it, logout works by recording the time a member was logged out; `verify()` now rejects any cookie whose session began at or before that time, while a fresh login afterward works normally. All 5 tests pass.

One thing worth flagging: `docs/adr/0001-keep-sessions-in-the-database.md` says sessions live in Postgres, but `sessions.py` has no database at all — it's purely a signed cookie. That pre-existing mismatch between docs and code wasn't something I could resolve without someone to ask, so I left it as-is and built the in-memory revocation mechanism consistent with how the code actually works today.
